Senaki Jewish Cemetery (Jewish section in Menji Municipal Cemetery)

Jewish Cemetery · Senaki, Georgia

Not demolished. Senaki, in western Georgia, developed as an important center after the 1871 Poti-Tbilisi railway connected it to the capital; the resulting settlement, originally called Akhalsenaki, became a city in 1921, was renamed Tskhakaia in 1933 after Soviet revolutionary leader Mikheil Tskhakaia, and reverted to Senaki in 1989. A small trading Jewish community formed in the early 20th century, growing from 40 people in 1910 to about 400 by 1939 and 741 by 1976, drawing migrants from Bandza, Kulashi, Vani, and Sujuna; by the 1970s, Senaki had become a significant center of Jewish life in western Georgia. A stone synagogue was built in 1880.
